lab: Analog and Digital Communications Virtual Lab
lab_display_name: Analog and Digital Communications Virtual Lab
introduction:
Analog and digital communication systems are fundamental to modern information transmission, enabling the reliable delivery of voice, data, and multimedia over communication channels. Their operation relies on concepts such as modulation, demodulation, spectral analysis, pulse modulation, digital signaling, multiplexing, and the effects of channel impairments. Although these concepts are introduced mathematically in lectures classes, understanding how the transmitted and received signals behave in the time and frequency domains is often easier through experimentation and visualization.
The Analog and Digital Communication Lab provides a simulation-based environment for exploring these principles through a sequence of eleven experiments. The sequence begins with mathematical and signal-analysis tools, including matrix operations and Fourier-based analysis, and then examines the statistical response of systems to wide-sense-stationary inputs. It proceeds to analog amplitude, frequency, and phase modulation; suppressed-carrier modulation schemes such as DSB-SC and SSB-SC; and pulse modulation techniques including PAM, PWM, PPM, and delta modulation. The digital communication experiments cover ASK, FSK, and BPSK generation and detection, including their passband implementations, followed by the study of channel effects and modulation schemes with memory such as MSK and GMSK. The final experiment addresses frequency/time-division multiplexing concepts.
Together, these experiments connect the mathematical representation of signals with the practical operation of communication-system building blocks. Students can observe modulation and demodulation processes, examine signal spectra, compare digital signaling schemes, and investigate how channel conditions influence system behavior. The lab is intended to complement classroom teaching with guided, hands-on simulation.

experiments.name: Understand various matrix operations, matrix decompositions, factorization, and related operations
Understand various signal processing tools like Fourier series, Fourier transform, Power spectral density, etc. for analyzing the signal
Study the statistical properties of the output response of a system when the input is wide-sense stationary
Analog amplitude, frequency, and phase modulation and demodulation with spectrum analysis
Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM), Pulse Width Modulation (PWM), Pulse Position Modulation (PPM), Delta Modulation, Pulse Coded Modulation & their Demodulation
Amplitude Shift Keying, Frequency Shift Keying, Binary Phase Shift Keying: Generation and Detection
Pass-band implementation of Amplitude Shift Keying, Frequency Shift Keying, Binary Phase Shift Keying: Generation and Detection
Study of the effect of the channel on the system with various modulations
Study of Modulation schemes with Memory, like MSK, GMSK, etc.
Study of Frequency/Time division multiplexed schemes

UG: The lab supports undergraduate courses in Analog Communication, Digital Communication, and Communication Systems. Its experiments provide practical simulation-based reinforcement of modulation and demodulation, signal spectra, pulse and digital modulation, channel effects, and multiplexing. The matrix and signal-analysis experiments also reinforce mathematical and signal-processing foundations relevant to these courses.

objective:
By the end of this virtual lab, learners will be able to:
  • Perform and interpret basic matrix operations and decompositions used in signal-processing and communication-system analysis.
  • Use Fourier-series, Fourier-transform, and power-spectral-density concepts to analyse signals in the time and frequency domains.
  • Understand the statistical response of systems driven by wide-sense-stationary inputs.
  • Generate and analyse analog AM, FM, and PM signals, and understand their corresponding demodulation processes.
  • Explain and investigate DSB-SC and SSB-SC modulation and detection.
  • Explore pulse modulation methods, including PAM, PWM, PPM, and delta modulation, and understand their demodulation principles.
  • Generate and detect ASK, FSK, and BPSK signals, and examine their passband representations.
  • Study how communication-channel effects influence transmitted signals and receiver performance.
  • Understand modulation schemes with memory, particularly MSK and GMSK, and their continuous-phase characteristics.
  • Develop an introductory understanding of frequency- and time-division multiplexing concepts.
